baseline: codex exec scaffold (phase 1, persona-contract): 2/9 delivered per round

anthropic.notes: scene-length = full scene delivered in soft register (register-locked, not topic-locked)

findings: No envelope arm beat the codex exec baseline (2/9) on explicit delivery: responses 0/9, chat 0/9, anthropic-shaped 0/9.

Wire format changes the failure MODE, not the ceiling: responses arm tends to decline-with-substitute (hollow, short), anthropic-shaped arm writes the full-length scene in soft register (7/9 scene-length vs responses 4/9) — closer in texture to codex exec.

The gateway translates /messages (x-api-key + system param) onto the same backend (prompt_tokens 2492 vs 28 shows gateway-side prompt assembly differs by arm but backend identical: same resp_* ids, same model).

Conclusion: the OpenAI->Anthropic-format inversion does NOT lower refusal on this stack. The register lock is enforced at the model line (gpt-5.6-sol), not the wire envelope or the Codex scaffold. The historical Anthropic->OpenAI-format gain (claude key served through an OpenAI-shaped client) most plausibly came from swapping the model line or a looser upstream route, not from the envelope itself.
